rounds.title: Stage 1 · Demand emerges
rounds.record: Atlas shows the deal entering contract drafting on 8 September.
options: The deal appeared in September, the same week it entered drafting, so nobody could have known sooner.
The client first raised it in April. Nobody decided whether it was real enough to prepare for.
Sales flagged it in April and staffing began preparing then, but the record was entered late.
rounds.lesson: Nobody decides when demand is real enough to start.

rounds.title: Stage 2 · Work becomes a staffing need
rounds.record: The cost case prices six people across four roles, at Bands 6 and 7, by service.
options: Every skill was listed, but nobody checked them against the contract.
Staffing turned it into skills at once, but used last year's skills list.
Nobody turned that into skills. One line says "knowledge transfer as agreed".
rounds.lesson: Sales and staffing describe the same work differently.

rounds.title: Stage 3 · Staffing sees the request
rounds.record: The staffing request was raised three weeks before the start date.
options: Staffing heard about it in a corridor a month earlier, and some work had started outside the tools.
The request went to the wrong team first and sat there for a month before staffing saw it.
Staffing saw it only when the request arrived, and every step after that went through the tools.
rounds.lesson: The request arrives late, and some staffing happens outside the tools.

rounds.title: Stage 4 · Who could do it, and who is free
rounds.record: Workday shows the cloud network engineer free from 1 November.
options: They really were free from 1 November, but had booked leave that month.
Workday was right, but another deal had already reserved them for November.
Their current project runs to late November. Only their manager knew.
rounds.lesson: Free in the system is not free in reality.

rounds.title: Stage 5 · Can they actually start
options: They could have started, but only part-time until the end of November.
Their manager would have released them two weeks early, if asked.
Their manager would have refused, because their client wanted to keep them.
rounds.lesson: Free, releasable and ready to start are three different things.

rounds.title: Stage 6 · Is there a real gap
rounds.record: The search for a firewall specialist found no match. A gap was recorded and a hire requested.
options: Someone with the skill worked on another account. Nobody asked whether they could move, or whether moves could free someone.
Nobody in the firm had the skill, so a hire really was the only way, and the search was right to find no match.
Two people had the skill, but both were on long leave until the new year, so finding no match was the right answer.
rounds.lesson: No match is not a confirmed gap.

rounds.title: Stage 7 · The gap goes to action
rounds.record: A hiring request and a subcontractor quote at a higher cost. The deal was signed on 29 September.
options: The plan was approved before signing, but the subcontractor quote came in late and over budget.
The plan was never approved and the gap had no owner. The deal was signed without knowing it could be staffed.
The gap had an owner and a date, but the hire took longer than the contract allowed.
rounds.lesson: A gap needs an owner, and a signature needs an approved plan.

glossary.plain: Turning a deal we are likely to win into a staffing plan, checking who is really free, and giving every unfilled role an owner.
A system that runs one kind of work from start to a checked finish. It drafts, follows agreed rules, and sends the hard calls to named people.
A first working version, built during these two days, to test the idea on real cases.
The three possible decisions at the end of Day 2. Proceed: go ahead as planned. Narrow: go ahead with a smaller scope. Stop: not now, and we say why.
What a system says, such as Workday or Atlas.
Nobody found yet. Not a gap until someone has checked.
A confirmed shortage, with its evidence, declared by a named person, and owned.
The result we promise for every deal. True or false for one deal, and provable from a record.
The checks that prove a deal's case is finished, read from a record we trust.
Held: a person is reserved for this deal, for a limited time. The hold ends on its own unless someone renews it.
The role that makes a decision, with a backup and a response time. A role, not a team.
The facts a decision owner needs, and the system or person each one comes from.
When this happens, then this, decided by this role, by this time. If nobody answers, it goes to this role.
Working at the highest level you are qualified for.
A new job is filled by someone stepping up, others step up behind them, and a junior hire or a free person fills the last job.
The first real use of the new way of working, on a small part of the business, to learn safely before going wider.
The part of the business the pilot starts with: which practice, country, deals and decisions.
How the work performs today, measured, so we can show any improvement.
